# Task: Fix Prefix Caching Producing Different Output on First Request vs Subsequent Requests on ROCm (MI355X)

## Issue
GitHub Issue: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/33123

On AMD MI355X GPUs (gfx950), vLLM with prefix caching enabled produces **different output on the first request (cache miss)** vs **subsequent identical requests (cache hit)**. The first request computes attention from scratch (full prefill), while subsequent requests reuse cached KV prefix (partial prefill + cached KV). These two computation paths produce numerically different results on MI355X, causing divergent outputs.

This bug does NOT occur on MI325X (gfx942), and does NOT occur on CUDA. It affects both `TRITON_ATTN` and `ROCM_AITER_FA` attention backends, so it is not attention-backend-specific. The issue is in the bf16 data flow specifically — fp16 works correctly.

## Reproduction

Using model `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` with bfloat16 dtype, prefix caching enabled, `--enforce-eager`:

| Request | Cache Status | Output |
|---------|-------------|--------|
| Run 1 | Cache miss (full prefill) | `'The European Union consists of 27 member states'` |
| Run 2+ | Cache hit (partial prefill + cached KV) | `'The European Union (EU) consists of **2'` |

The divergence occurs at token position 3, where the logprob difference is large enough to flip the argmax selection.

Without prefix caching, all runs produce identical output (confirming the bug is in the cache-hit path).

- vLLM+PC Run 2+ differs from Run 1 (cache hit path diverges)
- Issue is in bf16 data flow only — fp16 passes
